---
title: "exploring CP plot data"
output: html_document
---
```{r}
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```



```{r}
CP_plots_clean <- read.csv(here("species list data", "CP plots clean.csv"))
```

```{r}
# Step 1: Get top 10 families by total species count (across AR + NR)
top_families <- CP_plots_clean %>%
  group_by(family) %>%
  summarise(total_count = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_count)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  pull(family)

#collapse other families into 'other'
CP_plots_top_families <- CP_plots_clean %>%
  mutate(family_grouped = ifelse(family %in% top_families, family, "Other"))

#summarise relative abundance per family_grouped and restoration type
summary_data <- CP_plots_top_families %>%
  group_by(restoration, family_grouped) %>%
  summarise(total_abundance = sum(relative_abundance_percent, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

#plot the data
ggplot(summary_data, aes(x = restoration, y = total_abundance, fill = family_grouped)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("AR" = "Actively restored", "NR" = "Naturally regenerated")) +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Relative Abundance (%)",
    fill = "Family",
    title = ""
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5))
```





```{r}
#now I want to plot the actual number of species in the two sites, from the top 10 families
summary_data_counts <- CP_plots_top_families %>%
  group_by(restoration, family_grouped) %>%
  summarise(total_species_count = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(summary_data_counts, aes(x = restoration, y = total_species_count, fill = family_grouped)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("AR" = "Actively restored", "NR" = "Naturally regenerated")) +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Number of individuals",
    fill = "Family",
    title = ""
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5))

```
